- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive price drops or spikes), model should adjust forecast toward historical mean, not extreme extremes.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), forecast should be capped at +5% above peak to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), forecast should be anchored to recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.  
- Forecast should not lag true price by more than 2–3 days unless sentiment is strongly bearish — otherwise, adjust for momentum.  
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–5% to reflect sentiment reversal.
